{{Quote|In many ways, Bakura reminds me of Alderaan.|Leia Organa|<ref name="TaB" />}}
'''Bakura''', known in [[Ssi-ruuvi]] as '''Xwhee''', was a rich, green and blue [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Bakura system/Legends|Bakura system]] of the [[Shiritoku Spur]], located in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], and was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the indigenous [[Kurtzen]] and isolated [[Human/Legends|human]] colonizers known as [[Bakuran]]s. The native language of [[Kurtzen (language)|Kurtzen]] was spoken alongside [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].

Bakura's capital city, [[Salis D'aar/Legends|Salis D'aar]], was known as an important [[spaceport]] and financial center in the [[Bakura sector/Legends|Bakura sector]], while the planet itself served as one of the largest commercial hubs in Wild Space.

It was also the site of a historic truce between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] immediately following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], shortly before the [[Invasion of Bakura]].

==Description==
Bakura, which [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Bakura (star)|Bakura]],<ref name="TEA" /> was the third of eight [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the [[Bakura system/Legends|Bakura system]],<ref name="TTABSB" /> which was itself part of the [[Bakura sector/Legends|Bakura sector]] of the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was situated on the [[Shiritoku Way]], a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] that connected it to [[Timora]]<ref name="TEA" /> and was on the outer edge of the [[Shiritoku Spur]].<ref name="TEA" />

Bakura, a terrestrial world with a diameter of 21,400 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], possessed two [[Moon/Legends|moons]],<ref name="TEA" /> a moderate hydrosphere, and [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] 1.05 times standard and was the only world in its system with a breathable [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. Its climate was temperate and tended to be mild, with abundant cloud cover and high levels of rainfall.<ref name="TTABSB" />

Bakura's terrain included forests, plains, mountains, and some urban centers. The planet's three major continents were [[Braad]], [[Prytis]], and [[Kishh'daar]]; in the western hemisphere, Prytis and Braad both featured [[namana]] plantations, and Prytis also boasted an abundance of arable land, extensive agricultural regions, and mountain ranges with mines and quarries. Kishh'daar was in the eastern hemisphere.<ref name="TTABSB" />

Bakura's primary industry was the manufacture of [[Repulsor coil/Legends|repulsorlift coils]]; the production of tools and furniture using these coils was a secondary industry. The refinement of raw metals and minerals mined from the planet's two moons provided another industry, while the native namana [[Tree/Legends|tree]] helped the planet develop a significant agricultural sector.<ref name="TTABSB" /> The world exported repulsorlift coils and namana-based products while importing medicine and technology.<ref name="TEA" />

General disapproval of [[Droid/Legends|droids]], combined with high tariffs, led to a nearly total absence of droids on Bakura; droid technology was prohibited, and the possession of droids was only allowed with official permission and several permits. [[Repulsorlift generator/Legends|Repulsorlift generators]] were extremely common on Bakura.<ref name="TTABSB" />

Bakura's terrain mostly comprised mountains, valleys, plains, and small seas, all of which received a great deal of rain. Bakura's primary exports included strategic metals.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TEGtPaM" /> The planet was also the origin of a disease called [[Bakuran fever bump]]s.

==History==
{{Quote|We have come to restore you to your natural place in the galactic balance, and hope you will help us achieve this goal.|Captain Brellar welcomes Bakura into the Galactic Empire|<ref name="J5">{{JournalCite|5|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>}}
Bakura was first settled around [[150 BBY/Legends|150 BBY]] by the [[Hemei IV]]-based<ref name="TEA" /> [[Bakur Mining Corporation]], an exploratory mining consortium that sought to develop the planet's [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] and metal deposits. The first Bakuran settlers arrived equipped with food, seeds, tools, and some advanced building materials, although they hoped to use the planet's considerable natural resources to survive.<ref name="TTABSB" />

As was typical in colonization efforts, the Bakurans relied on droids, especially labor drones, to assist in the construction of homes and buildings. However, the droid complement of the [[Colony ship/Legends|colony ship]] had been sabotaged by the [[H'Lokk Consortium]], a rival of the Bakur Corporation that aimed to cause enough hardship for the Bakur Corporation's colonists to force their withdrawal from Bakura, allowing a nearby H'Lokk colony to annex the planet.<ref name="TTABSB" />

The H'Lokk Consortium's saboteurs introduced a minor virus into the Bakuran colonists' labor droids. The virus program was intended to force the droids to sabotage as many colony operations as possible, but an error in the program's code removed many of the droids' fail-safes, wiping out non-aggression mandates. During the early [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] of colonization, the droids successfully planned and carried out a [[Droid Uprising|revolt]], killing nearly 40% of the original colonists. The uprising was ultimately put down, and [[Deredith Arden]], the captain of the original colony ship, served as the first head of the Bakur Corporation government.<ref name="TTABSB" /> Since then, droids never enjoyed much trust on the planet.<ref name="TEA" />

Deredith Arden served as [[Prime Minister (Bakura)|Prime Minister]] for eight years, and under his leadership, the Bakura colony overcame a shortage of labor, established a mining operation, and constructed processing and manufacturing facilities. In [[146 BBY]], the Bakur Corporation chartered Bakura as a self-sufficient mining community. Initially, Bakura exported few goods to the rest of the galaxy, and its significant trading partners were limited to a small number of nearby worlds; nevertheless, it achieved a favorable economy.<ref name="TTABSB" />

The Bakur Mining Corporation's colonization of Bakura was considered the official founding of the planetary civilization. At first, the Corporation directly controlled the planet, but after Arden's death and faced with lessening returns of the [[Mining/Legends|mining]] operations and an increase of both population and wealth, a government comprising a [[Prime Minister (Bakura)|Prime Minister]] and a [[Bakuran Senate|Senate]] was established. However, this system of government was not truly representative; the titular head of government was always one of Arden's descendants, and the Senate elected its members. The Prime Minister, however—at least after the reforms following the [[Invasion of Bakura]]—was elected by popular vote.

[[File:JKAlevelshot_t1_fatal.png|thumb|left|A [[Bakuran power station]] with one of the moons looming large in the sky.]]
In [[97 BBY]], there was a major [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Droid Uprising|uprising]] on the planet, thus explaining the [[Anti-droid sentiment/Legends|aversion]] many of the planet's inhabitants felt for the automata.<ref name="TTABSB" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], during the Clone Wars, although neutral in the conflict and independent of both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a Separatist base was, for a time, established on Bakura. Shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]], [[Dooku/Legends|Count Dooku]] hid on Bakura, where he was engaged by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] and [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]], with the latter falling to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="Trackdown">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Trackdown]]''</ref> Around this time, the Separatist forces also [[Attack on Bakura|defeated]] the Republic on Bakura using the [[Force Harvester]].<ref name="TCW game">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (video game)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' video game]]</ref>

Seven standard weeks after the Battle of Geonosis, [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi Generals]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] [[Battle of Bakura (Clone Wars)|fought]] on Bakura against Separatist forces led by the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]. [[Unidentified traitor|A traitor]] in the Bakuran government made it possible for Grievous to [[Death/Legends|slay]] the entire [[Ruling Synod]].<ref name="Wild Space">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref> Bakura was opened to outside settlement<ref name="TEA" /> during the final years of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], after which immigration caused the population to triple within a decade. In spite of Bakura's demographic and economic advantages, [[Politics/Legends|political]] infighting prevented the [[Bakuran Senate]] from governing effectively, and for decades, Bakura's social and economic issues were ignored.<ref name="TTABSB" />

Bickering among the ruling upper class of the Corporation and the local Senate had always been an issue but grew stronger as the years went on. It reached the point where the Bakuran Senate could not agree on matters as simple as school schedules, and it was believed that the planet was near to civil war. Combined with the fact that the Senate directly controlled the small planetary military and that there was a sense of unrest among the people, Bakura was an easy target for [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] forces.

Bakura eventually became known as a successful producer of repulsorlift coils, which attracted the attention of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="TEA" /> In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], early on the night of [[Great ReSynchronization|36:1:1]], two [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] and supporting vessels neutralized the planet's defense grid. Subsequently, Imperial troops shuttled to the planet's surface and moved to seize strategic assets, facing negligible resistance. Several Imperial troopers became casualties as they attempted to secure the Bakuran Senate, but resistance ceased as members of the Senate were placed under house arrest.<ref name="J5" />

The [[Human/Legends|Human]] inhabitants of Bakura maintained a modest economy by exporting repulsorlift coils to the Empire. Annexation by the Empire allowed Bakura to send more goods to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and other regions, greatly improving Bakura's economy and causing the cost of importing goods to fall. The government of Bakura remained intact, but Prime Minister [[Yeorg Captison]] and the Senate were made answerable to Imperial Governor [[Wilek Nereus]]. Purges and two brief rebellions, which prompted further purges, ensued, but the Empire was entrenched as the true authority on Bakura. Much of the output of the planet's mines was diverted to the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star project]] at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="TTABSB" />

An [[Bakura Imperial Prison|Imperial Orbital prison]] was also stationed around Bakura. In approximately 3 ABY, it contained miscellaneous enemies of the Empire and several Rebel prisoners from the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. Thanks to the intervention of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] under [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], flying a [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighter]], he was able to disable several [[Imperial Action transport|Imperial transports]] with the B-Wing's [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] and allow for an Alliance [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75]] transport to evacuate the prisoners. However, one of his wingmen was hit by a [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE starfighter]], whose laser cannons shredded his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-Wing's]] stabilizer, causing him to crash land onto Bakura, inside Imperial territory. Antilles, thinking quickly, infiltrated the prison, commandeered a [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]], and flew down to rescue his wingmate. The two returned to orbit just in time to see an [[Imperial escort carrier (storm commando)|Imperial escort carrier]] leap into hyperspace with some scientists captured from rebel transports. General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]] extrapolated the escort carrier's course and estimated that the craft would head for [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], leading to a [[Battle of Geonosis (Galactic Civil War)|battle there]].

Although there was a short period of violent resistance to the Imperial occupation, and there were several Imperial purges of suspected (and actual) Rebel partisans, the vast majority of Bakurans were ambivalent about the Imperial occupation (perhaps partly fuelled by their passive religion). They acknowledged that Imperial control had ended their near-disastrous infighting, and their major gripe was the increased taxation. At the time of the Invasion of Bakura, the formal (and not very active) [[Bakuran resistance]] numbered only about one hundred individuals.

[[File:Salisdaar.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Salis D'aar/Legends|Salis D'aar]], capital city of Bakura.]]
The day following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], which saw the death of [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] and the shattering of his Empire, Rebel forces stationed on the Sanctuary Moon received a message droid from Bakura requesting help. Bakura was being attacked by the [[Ssi-ruu]]k—a saurian species from the most distant reaches of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], which attempted to establish a beachhead for an invasion of the known galaxy. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] dispatched a small task force led by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to assist in the defense of Bakura. Once the task force [[Bakura Trace/Legends|reached]] Bakura, a temporary truce was agreed to between the Rebels and the Imperials. In the end, the Ssi-ruuk were repelled, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperials]] in control of the planet were overthrown, and Prime Minister [[Yeorg Captison]] resumed control of the government. After his resignation, [[Gaeriel Captison]], niece of Yeorg and an important figure during the Ssi-ruuk invasion was elected to replace him.

Though the Ssi-ruuk had been defeated, Bakura could not let down its guard against another invasion, and the [[Bakuran Defense Fleet]] was formed as a result. They also developed four powerful warships. These were the three [[Bakura-class destroyer|''Bakura''-class Destroyers]]: ''[[Watchkeeper]]'', [[Defender (Bakura-class)|''Defender'']], and [[Sentinel (Bakura-class)|''Sentinel'']], and the [[Namana-class light cruiser|''Namana''-class Light Cruiser]] [[Intruder (Namana-class)|''Intruder'']]. These warships were equipped with [[Hyperwave inertial momentum sustainer|Hyperwave sustainers]] that allowed them to move through interdiction fields. These four warships were essential in maintaining a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] presence in the [[Corellian sector/Legends|Corellian sector]] during the [[Corellian Crisis|First Corellian Insurrection]]. Though this mission was successful, half of the fleet—the ''Watchkeeper'' and the ''Intruder''—was destroyed, and Gaeriel Captison was killed.

[[File:Bakura_JA.png|thumb|right|Bakura during the [[Disciples of Ragnos]] crisis]]During the [[Disciples of Ragnos]] crisis, [[Jaden Korr]] went on a mission with [[Kyle Katarn]] to Bakura to prevent a terrorist takeover of a power station. Kyle, however, did not show up, so Jaden decided to investigate the station alone. He found out that the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] was operating in the area and had armed several bombs throughout the station. Jaden battled the Remnant troops and deactivated the bombs before they could go off. Having completed his mission and reclaimed the station, Jaden left the planet in one piece.

While the Shiritoku Spur never joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Bakura was represented in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] by honorary Senator [[Molierre Cundertol]] during the [[Black Fleet Crisis]], although he was a non-voting member.<ref name="TEA" /> However, the planet withdrew itself from the New Republic and reasserted its independence before [[18 ABY/Legends|18 ABY]].

Later, during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Ssi-ruuk, once more, attempted to invade Bakura, armed with new entechment technology. They would use the deception that the [[P'w'eck]]s under the mutant Ssi-ruuvi, the [[Keeramak]], had toppled the [[Ssi-ruuvi Imperium]] and had come to Bakura to form an allegiance with the Bakurans. The [[Keeramak]] "consecrated" Bakura during a ceremony at the Bakuran Senate, thus allowing the Ssi-ruuk to fight on Bakura since they feared dying on unconsecrated worlds. However, their plan backfired when the [[P'w'eck]]s under [[Lwothin]] revolted against the Ssi-ruuvi and joined forces with the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] to drive away the Ssi-ruuvi during a [[Battle of Bakura (28 ABY)|second battle]]. It was revealed that Bakuran [[Prime Minister (Bakura)|Prime Minister]] [[Molierre Cundertol]], the former [[Senator/Legends|Senator]], had betrayed his planet. Despite this turn of events, Bakura initially chose not to join the Galactic Alliance. However, with the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] making new strides with the destruction of the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], Bakura joined the Galactic Alliance, contributing ships to the [[Defense of Mon Calamari (Yuuzhan Vong War)|defense]] of [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]] and giving the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Fleet]] access to the [[Hyperwave inertial momentum sustainer|HIMS]] technology for use during the [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar]].

==Society==
[[File:Bakura_Symbol.jpg|thumb|left|Symbol of the Bakuran government.]]
Bakura's only native [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was the [[Kurtzen]], a pale, hairless humanoid species, although its most populous sentient species was [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists (who composed the other 95% of the population). Other [[Alien/Legends|non-human]] species were a rare sight on the planet, and the inhabitants were suspicious of them.<ref name="TEA" />

Most Bakurans were independent-minded, insular, touchy and proud of their planet. Much of the population followed the Religion of the [[Cosmic Balance]], introduced by its Hemeian settlers.<ref name="TEA" /> The Balance flowered as a faith under the hierophant [[Dif Istuvi]]. Dif wrote its sacred text, [[Fulcrum (text)|''Fulcrum'']]. He also founded the order of priest prophets known as [[Zanazi]].

They were especially conscious about whoever descended from the original settlers, and whether they were followers of the Balance; these details had to be known in almost every new acquaintance.<ref name="TEA" />

Families who counted themselves among the Faithful had pairs of children close in age that followed the [[Rule of the Feather and Bowl]]. When each pair was a teenager, they underwent tests. The most promising youth obtained a small feather, while the other was given a golden bowl. The Child of the Bowl left home to join a communal Simple Home, serving the Zanazi. The Child of the Feather stayed as a part of Bakuran society and was given Zanazi funds for a more prestige education. Some Children of the Bowl left the Faith, but most submitted to a lifetime of service.

The native Kurtzen, however, followed their mystical faith, which featured totems and symbolism.

A droid rebellion engineered by the [[H'Lokk Consortium]] caused the death of many Bakurans. This left them with a distrust of machinery, which was banned from public use. Despite this, Bakurans were known for their repulsorlift industry, [[Bakur RepulsorCorp]]. Besides the Kurtzen, Bakurans did not know of any other alien species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. This made many Bakurans fearful and prejudiced against non-human species, a tendency only perpetuated during their time under Imperial rule.

Bakurans were masters of [[Organ replacement/Legends|organ replacement]], explaining why so many of them lived far longer than most Humans throughout the galaxy; for example, in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], [[Eppie Belden]] was 132 years old and still young enough to personally lead a guerrilla uprising.

==Locations==
[[Salis D'aar/Legends|Salis D'aar]], the capital [[City/Legends|city]] of Bakura, was located atop [[D'aarmont]], an immense outcropping of [[Quartz/Legends|quartz]] at the confluence of two rivers. Bakura's main [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] was located just south of Salis D'aar and on D'aarmont, and an Imperial garrison base identical to those found on many worlds was located a kilometer south of the spaceport.<ref name="GATORW" />

==Behind the scenes==
Many sources seem to place Bakura in the Outer Rim Territories—the ''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]'' identifies Bakura as being "on the outer edge of the Outer Rim Territories," the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' and the subsequent ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' claim Bakura is "located on the isolated edge of the Rim Worlds," ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]'' names Bakura as a "colony world in the Outer Rim" and "the Outer Rim planet Bakura," and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places Bakura "at the edge of known space." However, ''Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds'' explains that Bakura is located in the Shiritoku Space, an "area [that] remained formally part of Wild Space" following the [[Bakura Incident]]. The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Bakura in the [[Orus sector/Legends|Orus sector]], which is actually a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] located in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]].

''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' states that Bakura's gravity is "standard," while ''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]'' rates it at "1.05 standard."

In [[George Lucas]]' rough draft script for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] refers to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] as "the young hero of Bakura".<ref name="Making of">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>
